data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash -l
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -J planczos
#   -o planczos.out
#   -e planczos.err
#   -t 20
#   -n 8
#   -N 1
#   --mem-per-cpu=4000

#flux: --job-name=planczos
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 8
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=20m
#flux: --output=planczos.out
#flux: --error=planczos.err

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=4000
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

module load gcc/9.3.0-fasrc01 openmpi/4.0.5-fasrc01

PRO=planczos

# Slurm used srun --mpi=pmix; under Flux, use flux-run.
# Performance implication: if your MPI build requires a specific PMI/PMIx selection, site-specific settings may be needed.
flux run -n 8 -c 1 ./${PRO}.x > ${PRO}.dat

reasons: The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu=4000`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH -J planczos
#SBATCH -o planczos.out
#SBATCH -e planczos.err
#SBATCH -t 20
#SBATCH -n 8
#SBATCH -N 1
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=4000

# Set up environment
PRO=planczos

# Load required software modules
module load gcc/9.3.0-fasrc01 openmpi/4.0.5-fasrc01

# Run program
srun -n $SLURM_NTASKS --mpi=pmix ./${PRO}.x > ${PRO}.dat
